title: Enjoy by letting go
hookLine: all this is pervaded by the Lord; enjoy by renouncing, and do not covet (Isha Upanishad 1)
tomorrow: verse one says let go. verse two says live a hundred years. which?

cards: What would you do with a billion dollars? It's a game people play in group chats, and the answers get very specific: the house, the island, the dog with its own staff.

An Upanishad tells of a woman who was offered real wealth and asked a better question. The sage Yajnavalkya was about to leave home for the forest, and he offered to divide his property between his two wives.
One of them, Maitreyi, said: if this whole earth full of wealth were mine, would it make me immortal?

teach.h: NO HOPE OF THE DEATHLESS THROUGH WEALTH.
teach.b: No, he says. Your life would be like the life of the rich. There's no hope of the deathless through wealth.
And Maitreyi answers: then what should I do with something that won't make me immortal? Tell me what you know. So he does.

teach.h: DEAR FOR THE LOVE OF THE SELF.
teach.b: It isn't for the love of a husband that a husband is dear, he tells her, or a wife, or children, or wealth. It's for the love of the Self. Things are dear because of what shines through them.
Now the verse that opens the Isha Upanishad, which says the same thing in one breath.
All this, whatever moves in this moving world, is pervaded by the Lord.
Enjoy it by letting it go. Do not covet anyone's wealth. Notice the turn: the verse doesn't say give it all up and suffer.
It says enjoy, and the way to enjoy is to stop clutching. The verse says the world is the Lord's. One way to picture it is a guest at a feast: free to taste everything, owning none of it.
You can see that shape in prasad, food offered at a home shrine that comes back to the family as a gift, and in the Gita's line that those who eat what remains of the offering are freed.
Maitreyi set the wealth aside, and kept the better question.

how: The Isha Upanishad's first verse is chanted and studied by Hindus, and in Hindu homes food offered at the shrine is received back as prasad, a gift.

games.q: what does “enjoy by letting go” mean?
o: save your treats now so you can enjoy them later
give everything away and refuse all pleasure
relish the world without clutching it as yours

games.q: the forest, the wealth, the verse: tap the pairs.
p: the sage leaving for the forest
offered food received back as a gift

s: the Isha's first verse says to give up enjoying the world
it says enjoy: the way to enjoy is by letting go, without coveting.
Maitreyi asked whether wealth could make her immortal
in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad she asks what use wealth is if it can't do that.
Yajnavalkya tells Maitreyi a husband is dear for his own sake
he says the opposite: not for the husband's sake, but for the love of the Self.

games.q: your grandmother gives you her good china. you're scared to use it in case it breaks. what would the Isha say?
o: use it and enjoy it, as a guest of the Lord's world, without clutching.
lock it away; letting go means you shouldn't enjoy nice things.
sell it; owning anything precious is coveting.
games.why: the verse says enjoy, by letting go. not by locking up, and not by refusing the gift.

practice: Pick up one thing you own and love: a mug, a book, a ring. Look at it closely, its color, its weight, the small marks of use, the way a guest admires something in a host's house.
Enjoy it fully, and let the word mine go quiet while you do.

wordCard.voice: Enjoy by letting go: tena tyaktena bhunjitha, the Isha's first verse. The world is the Lord's; you enjoy it without clutching.

orig.note: Sanskrit, Isha Upanishad 1: enjoy by that renouncing.

carryVoice: A line for today: enjoy by letting go, like a guest at the feast. The Isha begins.

sources.ref: Isha Upanishad 1 (all this is pervaded by the Lord; enjoy by renouncing; do not covet anyone's wealth)
Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 2.4.1–5 (and 4.5) (Yajnavalkya, Maitreyi and the earth full of wealth; dear for the love of the Self)
Bhagavad Gita 3.13 (the good who eat what remains of the offering are freed)
